title: Fix the Method That Doesn't Actually Override
description: The program should have a Cat subclass override Animal's speak() method with its own sound. Fix the bug.
expectedBehavior: The program should print 'Meow', using Cat's overridden behavior.
actualProblem: Cat defines Speak (capital S) instead of speak (lowercase), so it's actually a brand-new method, not an override. Calling c.speak() still resolves to Animal's original method, printing '...' instead of 'Meow'.
explanation: Python method names are case-sensitive, and overriding requires matching the parent method's exact name. A subclass method with a differently-cased (or otherwise different) name simply adds a new method rather than replacing the inherited one.
